summary: Porcupine tower is named on two Saskatchewan lists at 52.62N, 101.83W; no source gives its build date, height or fate, and the reserve's towers are not linked to it.

evidence.supports: Tower list places the Porcupine tower at these coordinates
Canada Lookouts' Saskatchewan index lists a Porcupine tower
Porcupine Forest Reserve officially established as a national forest
evidence.quote: officially established the Porcupine Forest Reserve as a national forest

evidence.supports: Reserve established by the federal government in 1906
evidence.quote: In 1906, the Canadian government passed the first Dominion Forest Reserves Act
built a headquarters at Ushta, Saskatchewan

evidence.supports: Four fire towers built for the reserve's rangers, with cabins and stables
evidence.quote: In addition to the headquarters, four ranger cabins, five stables, and four fire towers were built for the rangers

evidence.supports: Canada Lookouts entry is the 1915 to 1916 report year
Four wooden lookout towers built in the Porcupine and Pasquia Reserve
evidence.quote: Porcupine and Pasquia Reserve - Four wooden lookout towers have been built and three are under construction.

evidence.supports: Those towers were 40 to 60 feet tall and near the ranger stations
evidence.quote: Most of these are from forty to sixty feet in height and are located in vicinity of the ranger stations.

notes_for_editor: Both lists give this tower only a name and coordinates. The brief's coordinates (52.62, -101.828) match the websiteservice entry. The Porcupine Forest material and the 1915 to 1916 Porcupine and Pasquia entry describe the reserve, not this tower, and no source links them. The story keeps one plain sentence saying the link is not confirmed; drop it if the editor wants no hedge. A firelookout.ca slug guess (porcupine-fire-tower) returned 404, so a record may exist under another slug and is worth checking. No photos found. No event has been recorded for this tower, because no source dates anything about it.
